work.text: Code that solves a security challenge. Two are active at this commit: bot_virus_v1, a bot that spreads across a test network, and ada_detection_v3, detecting commercial anti-detect browsers. A miner packages the solution as a Docker image, commits an encrypted pointer on chain, and it is revealed after 24 hours. What is paid for is a solution that scores above the previous best and is not a copy.
work.quote: The subnet incentivizes miners to develop and submit code solutions to various technical challenges, with a focus on enhancing security.

scoring.text: Per challenge, the validator runs the submission in a sandbox and gives a raw score from 0 to 1 against the previous best; below the challenge minimum, 0.85 for bot_virus_v1 and 0.5 for ada_detection_v3, it is not accepted. The penalty is the highest code-similarity score against other submissions. The final score is raw less penalty by a scoring algorithm, then decays linearly over 14 days.
scoring.quote: points decaying linearly over a 14-day period
scoring.disagrees: The docs root and the repository's docs/README.md say points decay linearly over 14 days; the dashboard concept page says decay starts once a submission is 10 days old and runs over approximately 10 to 15 days; the per-challenge managers that apply the decay run inside the challenge Docker images and are not in the repository.

split.text: Proportional within each challenge, then weighted across challenges: ada_detection_v3 carries 0.6 of the miner share and bot_virus_v1 0.4. Within a challenge each miner's decayed final score is normalised over all miners and only the best entry per entity is kept. A challenge with no scores has its weight redistributed to the others in proportion. No burn is applied in the code at this commit.

judges.text: Eleven validators were active on the 2026-09-09 chain snapshot, of 64 permitted. Weights are committed then revealed, at most once per 100 blocks. A validator decrypts each commit after 24 hours, pulls the miner's Docker image, runs it against the challenge container in its own sandbox with 4 CPUs and 12 GB, and calls a challenge scoring API. The loop that calls set_weights is not in the repository.
judges.quote: commit_reveal_weights_enabled True, weights_rate_limit 100, max_validators 64; chain-2026-09-09.json active_validators 11

cadence.text: Emission settles every 360 blocks, about 72 minutes. The validator's own epoch is 1,200 seconds, 20 minutes, and a commit is scored only once it is 24 hours old, the commit cooldown, so a new submission enters scoring a day after it lands. Submissions are scored once a day and a score fades over about two weeks. A new registration is immune from deregistration for 14,400 blocks, about 48 hours.

buyer.text: Nobody today. The front page promises a library of security solutions accessible to enterprises and the README says solutions can be integrated into real-world products, but there is no product page, API, price or named customer, and the site's copyright reads 2024. The miner's income is emission.
buyer.quote: A secure platform for 'red team' actors to earn TAO while competing against the best minds in the industry.

exploits.text: Copying: the penalty is the highest similarity to any other submission, past or same-day, identical re-submissions are rejected, and commits stay encrypted for 24 hours so a rival cannot copy inside the window. Many hotkeys for one operator: submissions sharing an IP, a Docker Hub username or a coldkey are grouped and only the best is paid. An earlier alpha-burn weight in the scoring is commented out.
exploits.quote: Keep only the best-scoring submission among miners that are considered the same entity.
